title: Azure multipart upload SAS must branch on credential type (account key vs token credential)
answers: Azure artifact multipart upload fails with DefaultAzureCredential
MLflow Azure Blob upload errors when logged in with Azure AD token credential
how does MLflow sign Azure block upload URLs without an account key
body:
Symptom: Artifact uploads to Azure Blob fail or are unusable for users authenticating with DefaultAzureCredential or another Azure AD token credential, because there is no account key.
Root cause: mlflow/store/artifact/azure_blob_artifact_repo.py:AzureBlobArtifactRepository.create_multipart_upload previously read self.client.credential.account_key unconditionally.
Fix pattern: Pick the SAS signing material by credential type. An account_key credential signs with account_key. A credential with get_token requests a user-delegation key via self.client.get_user_delegation_key(start, expiry) (start set 5 minutes in the past) and passes user_delegation_key plus start to generate_blob_sas. Any other credential raises _UnsupportedMultipartUploadException so the caller uses ordinary proxied upload.
Constraints: Shared-key SAS generation must stay unchanged. AzureSasCredential and None have neither attribute and must take the fallback, not attempt delegation.
applies: Applies to changes in the Azure Blob artifact repository's multipart/SAS code path; does not cover the proxied upload path itself.
says: Large artifact uploads to Azure storage fail when using Active Directory token authentication.
Cloud storage upload fails for users authenticated through enterprise identity credentials without storage keys.
Multipart file uploads to Azure Blob error out when logged in via single sign-on.
Support segmented artifact uploads to Azure storage using delegated identity credentials instead of keys.
Model artifacts cannot be uploaded to Azure when authenticating without account access keys.
search: In mlflow/store/artifact/azure_blob_artifact_repo.py:AzureBlobArtifactRepository.create_multipart_upload, Azure Blob multipart upload SAS URL generation must select signing material based on credential type. Credentials with account_key sign using the key, whereas token credentials providing get_token request a user-delegation key via self.client.get_user_delegation_key and pass it to generate_blob_sas. Credentials lacking both attributes, such as AzureSasCredential or None, must raise _UnsupportedMultipartUploadException from mlflow/exceptions.py to fall back to proxied upload.
